title: A fortiori from the Jewish Church — Christ and Paul reject extra-Scriptural traditions
source_text: XXVI. Primum ergo sic argumentamur. In Ecclesia Judaica, cum Scriptura sacra constaret solis Veteris Testamenti libris, tota salutis doctrina Scriptura continebatur, neque extabant ullae traditiones non scriptae aequalis cum Scriptura sacra authoritatis. Atqui multo magis credendum est totam salutis doctrinam hodie sacra Scriptura contineri, cum Scriptura jam aucta sit Novi Testamenti libris, in quibus exponitur doctrina Christi & Apostolorum. In Ecclesia vero Judaica non extitisse ullas traditiones non scriptas, ejusdem cum Scriptura sacra authoritatis, ex eo colligitur, quod, si quae tales habendae fuissent, proculdubio forent illae quas Judaeorum magistri commendabant, & quarum apud populum observationem urgebant. Sed illas vanas fuisse & hominum commenta docet Christus apud Matthaeum cap. 15. & apud Marcum cap. 7. Quum enim Scribae atque Pharisaei, qui tum erant Ecclesiae Judaicae Doctores, discipulos Christi arguerent, dicentes, Quare discipuli tui transgrediuntur traditionem seniorum? Non enim lavant manus quam panem edunt. Christus vicissim illos increpat, dicens, Quare & vos transgredimini praeceptum Dei per traditionem vestram? Item, irritum fecistis praeceptum Dei per vestram traditionem. Neque solum arguit eorum hypocrisin, quod mandatorum humanorum observationem urgerent, dum ipsi Dei mandata negligebant, & dogmatibus pravis corrumpebant: sed in genere declarat traditiones eorum tanquam frustraneas rejiciendas esse, nec ullas traditiones ut veras & legitimas a falsis & spuriis distinguit. Bene, inquit, de vobis prophetavit Isaias, sicut scriptum est, Populus iste labiis me honorat, cor autem eorum procul abest a me. Frustra vero me colunt docentes doctrinas quae sunt praecepta hominum. Nam omisso Dei praecepto tenetis traditiones hominum, lotiones sextariorum, & poculorum, aliaque similia hujusmodi multa facitis. Ideoque Paulus Coloss. 2. fideles monet ut sibi caveant ab hominum traditionibus, Videte, inquit, Ne quis vos decipiat per Philosophiam & inanem fallaciam, secundum traditionem hominum. Et Galat. 1. sibi ipsi vitio vertit quod ante suam ad Christum conversionem, Supra modum zelator fuerit paternarum traditionum. Cum ergo Christus & Apostoli damnent, ac pro doctrinis hominum habeant Judaeorum traditiones extra Scripturam sacram, pari ratione sequitur rejiciendas & damnandas esse traditiones Pontificiorum: cum illae non majori authoritate nobis commendentur quam Judaeorum olim traditiones.
pass_a_gloss: First, then, we argue thus. In the Jewish Church, when sacred Scripture consisted of the Old Testament books alone, the whole doctrine of salvation was contained in Scripture, and there existed no unwritten traditions of equal authority with sacred Scripture. And much more is it to be believed that the whole doctrine of salvation is today contained in sacred Scripture, since Scripture has now been enlarged by the New Testament books, in which the doctrine of Christ and the Apostles is set forth. But that there existed in the Jewish Church no unwritten traditions of the same authority with sacred Scripture is gathered from this: that if any such were to be held, they would doubtless have been those which the Jewish teachers recommended and whose observance among the people they pressed. But that those were empty and human inventions Christ teaches in Matthew chapter 15 and Mark chapter 7. For when the scribes and Pharisees, who then were the doctors of the Jewish Church, charged Christ's disciples, saying, Why do your disciples transgress the tradition of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread — Christ in turn rebukes them, saying, Why do you also transgress the commandment of God through your tradition? Likewise, You have made void the commandment of God through your tradition. Nor does He only accuse their hypocrisy, that they pressed observance of human commandments while they themselves neglected God's commandments and corrupted them by wicked dogmas; but in general He declares their traditions to be rejected as useless, and He distinguishes no traditions as true and legitimate from false and spurious ones. Well did Isaiah prophesy of you, He says, as it is written: This people honors Me with their lips, but their heart is far from Me. But in vain they worship Me, teaching doctrines that are the commandments of men. For laying aside the commandment of God you hold the traditions of men, washings of cups and pots, and many other such like things you do. And so Paul in Colossians 2 warns the faithful to beware of human traditions: See to it, he says, that no one deceive you through philosophy and empty deceit, according to the tradition of men. And in Galatians 1 he turns it against himself that before his conversion to Christ he had been exceedingly zealous for the traditions of the fathers. Since therefore Christ and the Apostles condemn the Jews' traditions outside sacred Scripture and treat them as doctrines of men, by like reasoning it follows that the Pontiffs' traditions are to be rejected and condemned: since those are not recommended to us with greater authority than the Jews' traditions once were.
pass_b_english: First argument: when Jewish Scripture was only the Old Testament, the whole salvation-doctrine was in Scripture, with no unwritten traditions equal to it.
A fortiori today: Scripture now includes the New Testament books that set out Christ's and the Apostles' teaching, so all the more must salvation-doctrine be contained in Scripture.

That Judaism had no equal-authority unwritten traditions follows because any such would have been the very traditions the Jewish teachers pressed — yet Christ shows those empty human inventions (Matthew 15; Mark 7).

When scribes and Pharisees (then the Jewish Church's doctors) charged the disciples with breaking the elders' tradition by unwashed hands (Matthew 15:2; Mark 7:5), Christ answered that they break God's commandment by their tradition and make God's word void (Matthew 15:3, 6; Mark 7:8-13).

He does not merely rebuke hypocrisy; He rejects their traditions as vain in general and draws no line between true and false extra-Scriptural traditions — citing Isaiah: This people honors Me with lips while the heart is far; in vain they worship Me, teaching human commandments (Isaiah 29:13 via Matthew 15:8-9; Mark 7:6-7).
Paul likewise warns against human tradition (Colossians 2:8) and recalls his own former zeal for ancestral traditions (Galatians 1:14).
So if Christ and the Apostles treat Jewish extra-Scriptural traditions as human doctrines, Rome's traditions fall the same way — they come with no greater authority.

choices.why: Classic a fortiori from OT-only to OT+NT canon.
